title: Welcome to Rotli
body:
# Welcome to Rotli

This is a real Markdown note in your vault. Edit it, experiment here, or delete it when you no longer need it.

## Things to try

1. Change this sentence and press **⌘S**.
2. Press **⌘N** to create a note.
3. Press **⌘K** to search notes, files, chats, and actions.
4. Type `/` on an empty line to explore Markdown blocks.
5. Select some text and ask Rotli about it in Chat.
6. Drop an image or file into **Assets**.

## Guided lessons

The **Welcome** folder in Main holds nine short lessons: writing, tasks, choices, tables, links, views, files, AI, and a checklist. Each one is an ordinary note with room to make mistakes. Click a control, then choose **Aa → Raw markdown** to see the same text underneath, and **Beautified** to return.

Edit the lessons, or delete the folder when you are done. Settings → General → Open welcome folder brings it back.

- [ ] Try a lesson
- [ ] Inspect its Markdown
- [ ] Delete what you do not need

## Your vault

- Your files stay in the folder you chose and work in other apps.
- **Library** is where Rotli organizes lasting notes.
- **Assets**, **Archive**, and **Trash** are system views of this same vault.
- This welcome note sits at the vault root, outside Library.

Make it yours.

title: Writing and formatting
body:
# Writing and formatting

Replace this sentence with something you want to remember.

## Make it readable

This is **bold**, this is *italic*, and this is `literal code`.

> A useful note starts with one clear thought.

- Capture the idea
- Add the detail
  - Keep related thoughts together

1. Choose one next step
2. Give it a little time

Try typing `/` on a blank line. Choose a heading, list, table, or code block. Use Aa → Raw markdown to inspect the source, then Beautified to return to the rendered view.

title: Tasks and progress
purpose: Click a control, inspect the source
body:
# Tasks and progress

Click these controls. Choose Aa → Raw markdown to inspect the state characters.

- [ ] Write the first draft
- [/] Review the details
- [x] Make room to think

Type `[]`, `[/]`, or `[x]` then Space on a fresh line. Enter continues with an unchecked task. Hover an open box and click **In progress** to mark it half done.

## Results

A result is a pass-or-fail answer. Click a box to choose it.

- [ ][ ] Did the check pass?
- [True][False] Is the decision ready?
- [True:green][Draw:yellow][False:red] What was the outcome?

- Type `[][]` then Space for a plain pass or fail pair.
- Type `[True][False]` then Space to name the answers. Any labels work, and three or more boxes are fine.
- Add `:color` after a label to pick its color, as in `[True:green][Draw:yellow][False:red]`. Typing the `:` opens a color list: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, brown, black, white, neutral, and accent. Press a number or click to choose. A hex value such as `[Yes:#E3B341]` also works.
- Click **+ reason** after a chosen answer to explain it in plain text, then undo the change.

Only ordinary tasks enter the vault's Tasks view. Results keep their own meaning.

title: Choices and toggles
purpose: Express a decision without losing the text
body:
# Choices and toggles

Adjacent circles make one choice. Squares are independent.

## One answer

Type `[#]` then Space on a fresh line, and again on the lines below it. Rows that touch form one group, so choosing one clears the others.

- [#] Small
- [#x] Medium
- [#] Large

## Several answers

Type `[##?]` then Space for the question, then `[##]` then Space for each option. The rows render as one panel. Hover the question and pick **Left**, **Center**, or **Right** to place the panel. That writes `[##?:center]` or `[##?:right]`; the bare `[##?]` sits at the left.

- [##?] What belongs in the first release?
- [##x] Writing
- [##] Advanced workflows
- [##x] Clear onboarding

## Switches

- [|x] Compact switch
- [True:green|x False:red] Ready to share
- [:blue|:green] A color-only switch

- Type `[|]` then Space for a compact green and red switch.
- Type `[True|False]` then Space to label both sides. Add `:color` after a label to color that side, as in `[True:green|False:red]`; the `:` opens the same color list.
- A color alone also works. `[:blue|:green]` reads as On and Off.

Select a different answer, then inspect the raw Markdown. Labels and selections remain plain text, and an `x` marks the chosen side.

title: Tables and code
body:
# Tables and code Click a table cell and change its text. Drag a column boundary to resize it. - To start a table, type `| Step | Owner |` on a fresh line and press Enter. Rotli adds the divider row and a first empty row; you never have to type the dashes yourself. - Press Shift+Enter inside a cell for a line break. The source keeps one row per line by writing `
` where the break is. - Shift-click a second cell to select a block of cells, or ⌘-click cells one by one. Delete clears them together, and ⌘C copies them as tab-separated text. | Step | Owner | State | | --- | --- | --- | | Draft | Me | Ready | | Review | Me | Next | | Share | Me | Later | ## Code remains code ```ts const nextStep = "Write one useful note"; console.log(nextStep); ``` Inline examples stay literal: `[#]`, `[##]`, `[True|False]`, and `- [ ]` do not turn into controls here. ```math E = mc^2 ```

title: Links and finding
body:
# Links and finding

Create another note with the title **My first idea** using New → Markdown note. Then come back to this lesson, type `[[`, and start typing its title. Pick it from the list and Rotli closes the link for you.

Literal example: `[[My first idea]]`.

Click the rendered link to open your note. Search for its title using the titlebar search field. Rename the note and check that the original title still resolves as an alias.

- [ ] Create My first idea
- [ ] Follow the link
- [ ] Find the note with search
- [ ] Rename and check the original link

An unresolved link should look unavailable. Rotli does not add pretend search results or vault notes.

title: Main and named views
purpose: One file, more than one way to reach it
body:
# Main and named views

Find this lesson in Main → Welcome and in All notes. They refer to the same file.

Use Main's view picker to create a named view. Add this note to it. Edit the note, return to Main, and check that you see the same edit.

- [ ] Create a named view
- [ ] Add this note to it
- [ ] Verify the edit from both places
- [ ] Remove the view and confirm the note remains

Remove a lesson from Main, then find it again in All notes. Move it to Trash, then restore it using the normal controls. Removing a reference and trashing a file are different actions.

title: Files and attachments
purpose: Try conventional formats on saved work
body:
# Files and attachments

These steps create real files. Start with disposable examples.

- [ ] New → Document: type a short paragraph, save, close, and reopen
- [ ] New → Sheet: enter values and a formula, save, close, and reopen
- [ ] New → Board: add a shape, save, close, and reopen
- [ ] On this note, attach an image and resize it
- [ ] On this note, attach a video and test playback
- [ ] Open a PDF and review its explicit editing or conversion path

Filesystem imports, native drops, and persistence must be tested in the Mac app. The browser twin cannot prove those behaviors. Complex imported documents should be checked against their source app after a save.

title: AI and privacy
body:
# AI and privacy

Writing works without a model. Chat and the Librarian are optional capabilities.

Use only disposable sample text for these checks. Connect a provider only when you choose to.

- [ ] Write and find a note while offline
- [ ] Review the Librarian setting and its explanation
- [ ] Create a secure test note and confirm remote AI cannot read it
- [ ] Lock a test note and confirm AI cannot edit it
- [ ] Inspect a saved chat as ordinary Markdown

Secure is an AI access boundary, not encryption at rest. Locked notes remain readable. Browser tests cannot prove Keychain, a provider's live behavior, or scheduled delivery.

title: Your launch checklist
purpose: Keep what helped, then make something real
body:
# Your launch checklist

Use this as a personal acceptance check. Keep the note if you want a durable record.

- [ ] I can create, edit, find, rename, trash, and restore a note
- [ ] I understand that Main and named views refer to the same files
- [ ] I can close and reopen tabs without losing work
- [ ] I can use my theme in both light and dark mode
- [ ] I can use the app in a narrow window and reach controls with Tab
- [ ] I know the Welcome folder is mine to edit or delete
- [ ] I tested native save and reopen in my disposable vault

Leave the Welcome folder whenever you like. Your own work starts with New → Markdown note.
